findings.what: sendViaResend only throws when the body has an `error` key. Resend does not use that shape: errors are `{statusCode,name,message}` with a 4xx/5xx HTTP status. Probe today: POST https://api.resend.com/emails with a garbage key returned HTTP 401 `{"message":"API key is invalid","name":"validation_error","statusCode":401}` and no `error` key (checked in node: has error key = false). So every failed send (bad key, unverified domain 403, 422 validation, 429 rate limit, 5xx) is returned as if it succeeded. /api/email/send then answers {success:true}, workflowEngine.js:164 and sdrEngine.js:433 record mail as sent, and sdrEngine.js:550 swallows errors with .catch(()=>{}). Emails can silently never leave the system.
findings.evidence_quote: Success response: { "id": "49a3999c-0ce1-4ea6-ab68-afcd6dc2e794" }  (errors per https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/errors carry an HTTP status plus name/message, e.g. 401 missing_api_key, 403 validation_error, 429 rate_limit_exceeded)

findings.what: The hard-coded fallback sender is `noreply@bmapzai.com`. DNS probe today against 8.8.8.8: `nslookup -type=NS bmapzai.com` -> Non-existent domain, and resend._domainkey.bmapzai.com is also non-existent. A domain that does not exist can never be verified in Resend, so any send using this fallback is refused (403). Combined with the error-handling bug above, this fails silently. Also backend/.env.example:29 documents `EMAIL_FROM=noreply@bmapzai.com`, but nothing in backend/src reads EMAIL_FROM (grep returned no hits); the code reads RESEND_FROM_EMAIL (emailSender.js:22, integrations.js:552), so an operator who follows .env.example leaves the real variable unset.
findings.evidence_quote: 403 `validation_error` - Various domain and testing restrictions (fetched summary of the errors page; sending from an unverified domain is refused)
findings.recommended_fix: 1) Set RESEND_FROM_EMAIL in Railway to an address on a domain actually verified in Resend (e.g. `Bmapz <noreply@YOUR-REAL-DOMAIN>`). 2) Change line 87 to `from: from || fromEmail` and add `if (!from && !fromEmail) throw Object.assign(new Error('RESEND_FROM_EMAIL is not set'), {code:'NO_FROM_ADDRESS'});` before the fetch. 3) In backend/.env.example replace `EMAIL_FROM=noreply@bmapzai.com` with `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=Bmapz <noreply@your-verified-domain>`.

findings.what: The idempotency row is inserted BEFORE the work (lines 45-47). Two paths then answer in a way that makes Stripe's retry useless: (a) line 116-119 returns 503 after the row exists, so Stripe's retry hits the duplicate-key branch (lines 49-52) and is acknowledged as 'already processed' -- the plan grant is never applied; (b) the catch at lines 214-216 only logs and falls through to `res.json({received:true})`, so any thrown error is acknowledged with 200 and never retried (the add-on grant failure is also swallowed at 93-95). Result: a paying customer can be charged and receive nothing, with no retry. Supabase calls at lines 133-180 also never check `.error`, so failed writes are invisible.
findings.evidence_quote: "A Stripe tenta entregar eventos ao seu destino por até três dias com um atraso exponencial no modo de produção." and "registre os IDs de evento que você processou e não processe eventos já registrados." (records IDs of events already PROCESSED, not before processing)
findings.recommended_fix: Add a helper `const unlock = () => supabaseAdmin.from('webhook_events').delete().eq('id', event.id);`. At line 117 call `await unlock();` before `return res.status(503)`. Change the catch at 214 to: `console.error(...); await unlock(); return res.status(500).json({ error: 'handler failed' });`. Check `.error` on every supabaseAdmin write in the handler and `throw` it so the catch fires. Alternative: insert the webhook_events row only after the switch finishes, with the unique key still guarding concurrent duplicates.

findings.area: Stripe webhook: subscription status vs DB constraint
findings.what: customer.subscription.updated writes Stripe's raw `sub.status` into subscriptions.status (lines 186-192). The table has `CHECK (status IN ('trialing','active','past_due','canceled','paused'))` (supabase/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:80; grep found no later migration changing it). Stripe also emits `unpaid`, `incomplete` and `incomplete_expired`. Those updates violate the constraint; supabase-js returns the error instead of throwing and the code never checks it, so the row silently keeps its old status. A subscription Stripe has moved to `unpaid` therefore stays `active`/`past_due` in Bmapz and access is never revoked.
findings.evidence_quote: "Quando uma assinatura mudar para `canceled` ou `unpaid`, revogue o acesso ao seu produto." (statuses listed: trialing, active, incomplete, incomplete_expired, past_due, canceled, unpaid, paused)
findings.recommended_fix: New migration: `ALTER TABLE subscriptions DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS subscriptions_status_check; ALTER TABLE subscriptions ADD CONSTRAINT subscriptions_status_check CHECK (status IN ('trialing','active','past_due','canceled','paused','unpaid','incomplete','incomplete_expired'));` Then confirm the access/credit gate treats `unpaid` and `incomplete_expired` as no access. In the handler: `const { error } = await supabaseAdmin...; if (error) throw error;`.

findings.what: resolvePriceId reads STRIPE_PRICE_ID_<PLAN>_MONTHLY / _ANNUAL / STRIPE_PRICE_ID_<PLAN> for the real plans (starter, growth, scale, enterprise; plan CHECK in 001_initial_schema.sql:78 and PLAN_MONTHLY_CREDITS in aiCredits.js:97-103). backend/.env.example:34-36 documents STARTER, PRO, ENTERPRISE only. `PRO` is not a plan, and GROWTH and SCALE are missing. An operator who follows the example gets HTTP 400 'price_id is required' (billing.js:56) when a customer picks Growth or Scale.
findings.evidence_quote: curl example: `-d "line_items[0][price]={{PRICE_ID}}"` -- a Price ID is required for every Checkout line item
findings.recommended_fix:
Replace the three STRIPE_PRICE_ID_* lines with:
STRIPE_PRICE_ID_STARTER_MONTHLY=price_...
STRIPE_PRICE_ID_STARTER_ANNUAL=price_...
STRIPE_PRICE_ID_GROWTH_MONTHLY=price_...
STRIPE_PRICE_ID_GROWTH_ANNUAL=price_...
STRIPE_PRICE_ID_SCALE_MONTHLY=price_...
STRIPE_PRICE_ID_SCALE_ANNUAL=price_...
STRIPE_PRICE_ID_ENTERPRISE_MONTHLY=price_...
STRIPE_PRICE_ID_ENTERPRISE_ANNUAL=price_...
and set the matching variables in Railway. Make the Stripe test case in integrations.js verify them (see the Stripe test finding).

findings.what: sendCompanyEmail accepts replyTo and forwards it to Gmail and SMTP, but both Resend branches (emailSender.js:19 and 22) omit it, and sendViaResend (82-91) has no reply-to field. Replies to mail sent through Resend go to the From address instead of the requested one. Resend's parameter is `reply_to`, not `replyTo`.
findings.evidence_quote: `reply_to` (accepts string or string array)  (as returned by the fetch of the send-email page)
findings.recommended_fix: Change the signature to `sendViaResend(apiKey, fromEmail, { to, subject, html, text, from, replyTo })`, add `reply_to: replyTo || undefined,` to the JSON body, and pass `replyTo` in both calls at lines 19 and 22.

findings.what: checkout.session.completed grants plan credits and add-ons without checking `session.payment_status` (lines 61-181), and there is no handler for checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded or async_payment_failed. The Checkout session created at paymentProviders.js:87 passes no payment_method_types, so whatever the Dashboard enables applies. If any delayed-notification method is enabled for BRL customers (the code stores amount_brl), a session can complete with payment_status 'unpaid' and credits are granted before the money arrives. Which methods are enabled in the Dashboard is not verifiable from code.
findings.evidence_quote: "Delayed payment methods generate a checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded event when the payment succeeds later" (PT original: "Formas de pagamento postergadas geram um evento checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded quando o pagamento é bem-sucedido posteriormente."); sample code: `if checkout_session.payment_status != 'unpaid'`
findings.recommended_fix: Right after `const session = event.data.object;` add `if (session.payment_status === 'unpaid') break;` and add `case 'checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded':` as a fallthrough label next to `case 'checkout.session.completed':` so the same grant runs once the payment lands. Add `case 'checkout.session.async_payment_failed':` to log/notify. Then in Dashboard > Webhooks add both async events to the endpoint. Simplest alternative: restrict Dashboard payment methods to instant ones (cards) until this is done.

findings.area: Stripe API version pin (no env override)
findings.what: `apiVersion: '2024-06-20'` is hard-coded in two places with no environment override: billing.js:23 and stripeWebhook.js:29. Stripe's current version is 2026-09-30.endive, so the pin is about two years and several major releases behind. I found no published sunset or end-of-life for 2024-06-20 (search of docs.stripe.com returned none), so nothing breaks on a date, but the pin cannot be changed without a deploy and the two copies can drift. Note: the pin only controls responses to outgoing API calls. Webhook payload shape is decided by the webhook endpoint's own API version (see the unverified finding).
findings.evidence_quote: "The current version is 2026-09-30.endive." and "Webhook events use the API version that's set during your webhook's endpoint creation. Otherwise, they use your Stripe account's default API version"
findings.recommended_fix: Create backend/src/lib/stripeClient.js: `export const STRIPE_API_VERSION = process.env.STRIPE_API_VERSION || '2024-06-20'; export const makeStripe = () => new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, { apiVersion: STRIPE_API_VERSION });` and use it in billing.js:21-24 and stripeWebhook.js:28-29. Do NOT bump to 2026-09-30.endive before go-live: stripe-node 16.x types and behaviour are tied to 2024-06-20. Plan the upgrade (SDK ^23 + new version string + new webhook endpoint per https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades) as a post-launch task.

findings.what: package.json has `"stripe": "^16.2.0"` (installed 16.12.0). Latest on npm today is 23.0.0 (dist-tags.latest). Stripe's policy says only the newest major gets fixes.
findings.evidence_quote: "Older major versions of the package continue to be available for use, but won't receive any additional updates."
findings.recommended_fix: Keep 16.12.0 for launch (pin it: `"stripe": "16.12.0"` to prevent surprise minor updates). Schedule the upgrade to ^23 together with the apiVersion change and re-test checkout, portal and webhook against Stripe test mode.

findings.what: constructEvent verifies the signature but does not care which API version rendered the payload. The handler reads session.customer/subscription/payment_intent/amount_total/metadata, sub.status/customer and invoice.customer, which I expect to be stable across recent versions but did not verify per version. The endpoint's own API version (Dashboard > Workbench > Webhooks) was not checked; I cannot see the Dashboard. If the account default is newer than 2024-06-20 the payload shape can differ from what the pinned SDK assumes.
findings.evidence_quote: "Webhook events use the API version that's set during your webhook's endpoint creation."
findings.recommended_fix: In the Stripe Dashboard open the webhook endpoint and read its API version. If it is not 2024-06-20, create a new endpoint with `api_version=2024-06-20` (or the version chosen after the SDK upgrade), subscribe it to: checkout.session.completed, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded, checkout.session.async_payment_failed, customer.subscription.updated, customer.subscription.deleted, invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed, and replace STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in Railway.

findings.area: Stripe webhook: renewals and plan changes
findings.what: The handler never processes invoice.paid and customer.subscription.updated only syncs `status` (lines 184-194). A plan change made in the Customer Portal (billing.js:96) never updates plan, credits or contacts_limit, so the customer pays for one plan and keeps another. Renewals are tracked by a fixed 30-day cycle (line 125) instead of Stripe's billing period, which drifts from the real invoice date.
findings.evidence_quote: "`invoice.paid` Enviado quando a fatura é paga. Você pode provisionar acesso ao produto quando recebe este evento e `status` é `active`."
findings.recommended_fix: In customer.subscription.updated, read `const priceId = sub.items?.data?.[0]?.price?.id;`, map it back to a plan with the same env vars used by resolvePriceId, and update plan/contacts_limit/ai_credits_total when it changed. Add `case 'invoice.paid':` that clears past_due back to active and (if desired) anchors cycle_ends_at to `invoice.period_end`. If plan changes are not allowed, disable plan switching in the Portal configuration instead.

findings.area: Resend test case: false negative for sending-only keys
findings.what: The test calls GET /domains (integrations.js:545) and treats any non-2xx as 'key rejected' (547). Resend API keys can be `sending_access`, which can only send. The domains list requires full access, so a perfectly good sending-only key is reported as rejected. Also, GET /domains returns 20 items by default (max 100) with `has_more`; a team with more than 20 domains can be told that a verified From domain is not verified (lines 560-565).
findings.evidence_quote: "Full access required. A sending-access API key cannot call this endpoint." (fetch summary of the page); create-api-key page: `sending_access`: "Can only send emails."; limit default 20, max 100
findings.recommended_fix: Change line 545 to `fetch('https://api.resend.com/domains?limit=100', ...)`. Before line 547 add: `if (!r.ok && d.name === 'restricted_api_key') return res.json({ success: true, message: 'Resend sending-only key accepted. Domain status cannot be checked with this key type; send a test email to confirm.' });` (restricted keys return error name `restricted_api_key` per https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/errors). Not probed with a real key (none exist).

findings.area: Stripe test case: can pass while billing cannot work
findings.what: The test cannot pass without a valid secret key (probed, see test_cases). But it returns success:true for a valid key plus ANY non-empty STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (lines 580, 586) and never checks the price IDs. So it can report green while checkout still returns 400 'price_id is required' or the webhook rejects every event. It also does not detect a live key paired with a test-mode webhook secret.
findings.evidence_quote: Stripe documents the endpoint signing secret as a value starting with `whsec_` ("um segredo de assinatura iniciado por `whsec_`")
findings.recommended_fix: After line 580 add: `const whsec = clean(process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET); const webhookSet = /^whsec_/.test(whsec);` and `const missingPrices = ['STARTER','GROWTH','SCALE'].filter(p => !(process.env[`STRIPE_PRICE_ID_${p}_MONTHLY`] || process.env[`STRIPE_PRICE_ID_${p}`]));` then include `missingPrices.length ? `missing price IDs: ${missingPrices.join(', ')}` : null` in `bits` and set `const ok = d.charges_enabled !== false && webhookSet && missingPrices.length === 0;`. Optional stronger check: GET https://api.stripe.com/v1/prices/<id> for each price ID.

findings.what: GET https://api.stripe.com/v1/account behaves correctly: no key -> 401, garbage key -> 401 `Invalid API Key provided: sk_test_******e123`, and an unknown path (/v1/accountzzz) returns 404, so the route exists. But the current API reference page I could fetch (docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/retrieve) documents only `GET /v1/accounts/{id}`, and docs.stripe.com/api/account/retrieve returned 404. I could not confirm in today's docs that the id-less form is still documented, so it may be legacy. Restricted keys (rk_) without account-read permission would also get a 403 and be reported as rejected.
findings.evidence_quote: "Retrieves the details of an account."  curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/accounts/{{ACCOUNT_ID}}
findings.recommended_fix: Low urgency. Keep the call for launch (works today). Add a `Stripe-Version: <STRIPE_API_VERSION>` header at line 576 so the test matches the pinned SDK. If Stripe ever removes the id-less route, switch to GET https://api.stripe.com/v1/balance (proves the key works; then drop the charges_enabled check or read it from /v1/accounts/<id>).

findings.area: Resend: no idempotency or rate-limit handling
findings.what: POST /emails has no Idempotency-Key header (emailSender.js:83-85), so workflow/SDR retries can double-send. Resend allows 10 requests/second per team; with the error bug a 429 is invisible, and loops such as sdrEngine.js:550 send sequentially with errors swallowed.
findings.evidence_quote: "The default maximum rate limit is 10 requests per second per team."  Idempotency-Key: unique per request, expires after 24 hours, max 256 characters (send-email page)
findings.recommended_fix: Add an optional `idempotencyKey` argument and header `...(idempotencyKey ? { 'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey } : {})`. After the fix to the error check, on `r.status === 429` wait for the `retry-after` header seconds and retry once. Use e.g. `workflow-${runId}-${stepId}` as key in workflowEngine.js:164.

findings.area: Stripe client construction when key is missing
findings.what: getStripe() always returns a client (billing.js:21-24, called at 62), so the PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED guard at paymentProviders.js:81 is unreachable. With STRIPE_SECRET_KEY unset I confirmed in node that `new Stripe(undefined, ...)` does not throw in 16.12.0; the failure shows up later as a raw Stripe auth error returned to the browser as a 500.
findings.evidence_quote: n/a (local behaviour verified with node: constructor with undefined key does not throw)
findings.recommended_fix: `async function getStripe() { if (!process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY) return null; const Stripe = (await import('stripe')).default; return new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, { apiVersion: STRIPE_API_VERSION }); }` The portal route at line 95 must then check `if (!stripe) return res.status(503).json({ error: 'Stripe is not configured' })`.

findings.what: success_url (billing.js:70) has no {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} placeholder, so the landing page cannot fulfil on its own if the webhook is delayed. And the webhook does all its Supabase writes before answering (lines 59-218), while Checkout waits for the webhook response before redirecting.
findings.evidence_quote: "Checkout waits up to 10 seconds for your server to respond to the webhook event delivery before redirecting your customer."
findings.recommended_fix: Change the default success URL to `${process.env.FRONTEND_URL}/billing?success=true&session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}`. Keep webhook DB work fast (single round trips), or acknowledge first and process in the background once lost-event handling (the webhook finding above) is fixed.

findings.what: `stripe.billingPortal.sessions.create({ customer, return_url })` matches my knowledge of the API, but I did not fetch the portal documentation today. Known prerequisite (not re-verified): a portal configuration must be saved in the Dashboard for live mode, otherwise the call errors and the route returns a 500 with the Stripe message.
findings.recommended_fix: Before go-live open Dashboard > Settings > Billing > Customer portal in LIVE mode, save the configuration (cancel, update payment method, and plan switching only if the webhook supports it), then test POST /api/billing/portal once with a real subscription.

findings.area: Gmail send and Meta Graph version
findings.what: Outside the Stripe/Resend scope and not audited today: Gmail users.messages.send call (emailSender.js:57; error parsing via `d.error` matches Google's error shape but I did not fetch docs) and Meta Graph version v25.0 in email.js:7 (has env override META_GRAPH_VERSION).
findings.recommended_fix: Cover in a separate Google/Meta audit pass.

findings.area: Stripe webhook raw body and signature verification
findings.what: express.raw is mounted on /api/stripe/webhook (index.js:137) before express.json (index.js:143), and the handler passes req.body (a Buffer) with the Stripe-Signature header to constructEvent (stripeWebhook.js:30). Failure returns 400. Duplicate delivery is guarded by event id. All consistent with Stripe's current guidance.
findings.evidence_quote: "A Stripe exige o corpo bruto da solicitação para realizar a verificação de assinatura."
findings.recommended_fix: None. Note: `Stripe.webhooks.constructEvent` also exists as a static function (verified in node), so the per-request `new Stripe(...)` at line 29 is unnecessary.

findings.what: Endpoint, method, host, auth and body match the current Resend docs: POST https://api.resend.com/emails, `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, JSON with from, to (array, max 50), subject, html/text. Success is `{id}`. Only the response handling is wrong (see the first finding).
findings.evidence_quote: "Endpoint: POST to https://api.resend.com/emails ... Authorization: Bearer re_xxxxxxxxx ... to: Recipient email (max 50 addresses as array or string)" (as returned by the fetch)
findings.recommended_fix: None for the request itself.

findings.what: Core parameters used in paymentProviders.js:87-97 (mode, line_items[price,quantity], success_url, cancel_url, metadata) match the current Checkout docs, and hosted_page is the default ui_mode so success_url is required and present. customer_email, subscription_data.metadata and the subscription-mode combination were not individually re-verified today.
findings.evidence_quote: "For Checkout Sessions with the default ui_mode of hosted_page, set the success_url."
findings.recommended_fix: None.

findings.what: package.json lists `"resend": "^3.4.0"` but no file imports it (grep for from 'resend', require and import('resend') found nothing); all Resend traffic uses fetch. Latest npm is 6.32.1. A dead dependency only adds install weight and audit noise.
findings.evidence_quote: npm view resend version -> 6.32.1
findings.recommended_fix: Remove `"resend": "^3.4.0"` from backend/package.json dependencies (and refresh package-lock.json).

test_cases.notes: Probed today. No key -> HTTP 401 (code returns 'Stripe secret key not set' before any call). Garbage key sk_test_garbage123 -> HTTP 401 {"error":{"message":"Invalid API Key provided: sk_test_******e123","type":"invalid_request_error"}}; code checks `!r.ok` so it fails correctly. Cannot report success without a valid key. Caveats: passes with a valid key and any non-empty STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and never checks price IDs (see finding); docs page for the id-less /v1/account form not confirmed.

Probed today. No key -> 401 {"statusCode":401,"message":"Missing API Key","name":"missing_api_key"}. Garbage key re_garbage123 -> 400 {"statusCode":400,"message":"API key is invalid","name":"validation_error"}; code's `!r.ok` branch fails both correctly, and no-key short-circuits at line 544. Caveat: false NEGATIVE for sending-only keys (needs full access), and only the first 20 domains are read.

Same behaviour as resend. The test checks key validity and From-domain verification but does not exercise POST /emails, so it would not catch the response-handling bug at emailSender.js:93. POST /emails probe: no key -> 401 missing_api_key; garbage key -> 401 validation_error; neither body contains an `error` key.
